# Question 1

Which ledger rows bind a commit SHA that is not reachable from origin/main, and what superseding row does each need?

## Context

Population is every 40-hex string in .ea/generations/gen-*/ledger/*.jsonl that resolves to a commit, tested with `git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> origin/main`; the roadmap expected 22 at its HEAD. Under decision D-8 no SHA binds before publish, and the ledger is append-only.

## What to deliver

List each unreachable SHA with the ledger file, record key and field that binds it, whether the commit still exists locally, and the superseding row (collection, fields) that would rebind it to its published equivalent. Report the count you measured and the command you used.

Which of the seven recorded git-history incidents would each D-8 gate have caught?

reply.text: Campaign CAM-0004 synthesis (ART-0008#r1, sha256:1edddba3845ba9f9b5f3f6a2c7c8c3b3 per view) and survey ART-0003#r1 (sha256:6abba17f79dc3e7ccb4f31d94c6d9da79bdc457f1b6eb430f5d9743aef9ef491): 22 committed ledger rows in the task snapshot bind a commit SHA reachable from neither origin/main nor feature/eawf-v0.7-rc2 (all 22 git-verified 2026-10-08, record .ea/local/rc2-evidence/2026-10-08-cr0375-reachability.txt). Each needs an appended same-key superseding row: 12 P22-P30 rows declare unreachable_shas, 10 P36-I01 rows rebind to their published equivalent. Never an in-place edit.

QST-0084.question: Can an in-place ledger SHA remap ever be legal under the append-only ledger contract?

reply.text: No. Campaign CAM-0004 step 6 (ART-0007#r1, sha256:d5c7ce30ea81d2983fc7b30d2ea9097407477f6f63439da82d9792dc07160582): an in-place ledger SHA remap is never legal; ledger.py write-once premise, verify_append_only and guarded_ledger_write refuse it, and the only legal correction is an appended row whose supersedes names the earlier line's digest.

After each Run, score it with `eawf bench dispatch <run> --check --tier fixture` (EAWF-0505) and write the result as a dispatch smoke receipt beside the canary receipts (src/eawf/workflow/release/canary_receipts.py:74-104); `provider_probe`, which `build_receipt_probes` binds (src/eawf/workflow/release/signal_probes.py:505-521), then fails until every claimed os_class (EAWF-0506) carries a passing receipt. Release preflight step, not a CI gate (live dispatch needs credentials, costs money, and macOS runners cannot sign in): run `EAWF_SMOKE_PROVIDER=claude uv run pytest -m e2e tests/e2e/test_smoke_milestone.py` with EAWF_SMOKE_EVIDENCE_DIR set, on Linux (bwrap) and on macOS (seatbelt); every Run must reach COMPLETED with a sealed candidate and pass the scorecard; commit the receipts. Add that step to the release-process block (src/eawf/platform/profiles/data/core.yaml:391-416) and re-render docs/rules/release-process.md with `eawf sync`. Ordered after the dispatch fixes so the smoke measures the fixed dispatch, and after EAWF-0472 and EAWF-0483, which also edit core.yaml. Eight files because the two provider suites gain smoke receipt fixtures.

response.object: exit 0 of the native field name test; proof locus src/eawf/kernel/store/kinds/agent_report.py (ExecutorReportBody, PlannerReportBody, OperatorReportBody)

criteria.text: The agent report bodies name native entities: `ExecutorReportBody.task_key` replaces `wave_id`, `PlannerReportBody.tasks` (items `PlannedTaskSummary` with `task_key`) replaces `waves` (`PlannedWaveSummary.wave_id`), and `OperatorReportBody.milestone_key` and `completed_task_keys` replace `phase_id` and `completed_wave_ids`; a new body naming any of the four epoch-1 fields is refused with `extra_forbidden`.

response.object: exit 0 of the stored-row upgrade test; proof locus src/eawf/workflow/agent_report/store.py

criteria.text: A stored report row written with the epoch-1 field names (an `.ea/store/<role>_report.jsonl` line or an imported legacy ledger row) still loads through the report store reader: the reader upgrades the row once, at the read boundary, to the native names with every value unchanged, and stored files are not rewritten.

response.object: exit 0 of the role page example test; proof locus src/eawf/surfaces/render/agents.py

criteria.text: Every typed report example on the shipped role pages (src/eawf/surfaces/render/agents.py) parses as `AgentReportBody` under the native names, so an agent copying an example sends a report the agent_end hook accepts.

response.object: exit 0 of the packaged-bundle census; proof locus src/eawf/workflow/skills/census.py (bundle_census)

criteria.text: The packaged plugin bundle census of EAWF-0473 (CR-0473-2) finds zero epoch-1 nouns once the role page examples use the native field names.

tasks.intent: Rename the epoch-1 field names of the typed agent report schema (src/eawf/kernel/store/kinds/agent_report.py) to native ones so the shipped role pages can show valid report examples without epoch-1 nouns: wave_id -> task_key (ExecutorReportBody; PlannedWaveSummary becomes PlannedTaskSummary), waves -> tasks (PlannerReportBody), phase_id -> milestone_key and completed_wave_ids -> completed_task_keys (OperatorReportBody). EAWF-0473 cleaned the role pages but left five hits that are live schema keys (CR-0473-2 stays red): renaming them only on the page would make agents send reports that agent_end validation rejects. Update every reader of the renamed fields (kernel/validate/invariants.py, workflow/agents/specs/models.py, workflow/dispatch/seed.py, workflow/agent_report/) and the role page examples, and keep stored rows readable by upgrading epoch-1 rows once at the read boundary instead of rewriting stored files. Regenerate the role page and subagent spec goldens with their own recipes. Ordered after EAWF-0473 (its pages and census test) and after EAWF-0489, which deletes surfaces/render/agent_report.py, the last renderer of these fields.

tasks.intent: Captured Run output on this machine also carries /run/user/<uid> runtime paths and pytest-of-<user> temp roots, which committed state never held. Anchor both in the shared leak set and withhold those lines with eawf store redact-content before the rc3 state commit.
tasks.title: Scrub runtime-directory and pytest temp-root paths from content

response.object: exit 0 of the escaped-prefix leak pattern test

criteria.text: The leak scan flags a server data-root, runtime-directory or pytest temp-root path that follows an escaped line break, tab or carriage return or an underscore, and still leaves a path after an alphanumeric or a dot alone.

response.object: exit 0 of path-leak-lint over the artifact ledger

criteria.text: No content row in the artifact ledger carries a machine path behind an escaped line break or an underscore.

tasks.intent: The server data-root, runtime-directory and pytest temp-root anchors use a lookbehind that counts the letter n and the underscore as word characters, so a path right after a JSON-escaped line break, tab or carriage return, or after an underscore, escapes both the content bound and the path-leak lint. Let those prefixes start a path while an alphanumeric or a dot before the slash still exempts it, then withhold any content row the wider scan newly flags with eawf store redact-content before the state commit.
tasks.title: Flag machine paths after an escaped line break or an underscore

response.object: exit 0 of the redaction-versus-WAL refusal test

criteria.text: eawf store redact-content refuses, and changes no ledger byte, while the native write-ahead log holds a pending or applied record whose ledger line targets the artifact ledger.

tasks.intent: Redaction rewrites an unpublished artifact-ledger line, but crash replay recognises a line only by its exact digest, so an applied or pending write-ahead-log record whose ledger line targets the artifact ledger re-appends the original leaked line at the next boot. Refuse eawf store redact-content with a typed REDACTION refusal code while any such record is unfinished, naming the record, so the operator lets recovery finish first.
tasks.title: Refuse content redaction while the WAL holds an unfinished ledger line

response.object: exit 0 of the mixed-ledger redaction test

criteria.text: A redaction plan over a ledger whose unpublished non-content line leaks still withholds every flagged content line and names each flagged non-content record key instead of refusing.

tasks.intent: A content redaction plan is refused whole when any unpublished non-content line of the artifact ledger matches a leak pattern, and the wider patterns now flag older plan and spike rows that no verb can fix. Withhold the flagged content lines anyway and list each flagged non-content record key in the answer so the operator can see what stays.
tasks.title: Redact content rows when a non-content line also leaks

response.object: exit 0 of the meter verb weighting test

criteria.text: For the same samples and cap, the budget meter verb returns the observed token total and cap verdict the native dispatch meter computes with the governor's cache_read_weight.

tasks.intent: The runtime.run.budget.meter verb folds samples with a meter at cache-read weight 1.0, while native dispatch meters the same Run with the governor's cache_read_weight, so the two disagree on whether a cache-heavy Run is over its cap. Build the verb's meter from the same governor weight dispatch uses.
tasks.title: Weight cache reads in the budget meter verb like dispatch

response.object: exit 0 of the quarantine refusal test

criteria.text: When the newest provider-fact row for a runtime and version is a quarantine, eawf release canary-export refuses that claim instead of exporting the earlier certification.

response.object: exit 0 of the expiry refusal test

criteria.text: eawf release canary-export refuses a certification whose expires_at is before the export time.

response.object: exit 0 of the re-export carry-forward test

criteria.text: A re-export of a release that already has an export keeps its isolation pair, its run_logs and the certifications of every os_class not exported this run.

tasks.intent: The canary export takes the newest row that carries a certification, so a later quarantine of the same runtime and version is skipped, an expired certification is copied as is, and a re-export of the same release keeps only its Milestones, dropping isolation, run_logs and certifications of os_classes not passed this run. Take the newest row per runtime and version whatever its outcome, refuse a quarantined or expired one with a typed reason, and carry the prior export's isolation, run_logs and other os_class records forward.
tasks.title: Export only live, unexpired certifications and keep prior evidence

response.object: exit 0 of the missing check document test

criteria.text: The provider gate fails a pass receipt whose run_refs lack a matching check document beside it.

response.object: exit 0 of the breached check document test

criteria.text: The provider gate fails a pass receipt when any of its check documents lists a breach or names another Run.

response.object: exit 0 of the remediation command test

criteria.text: The dispatch_smoke_missing remediation names EAWF_SMOKE_EVIDENCE_DIR and the provider of the runtime whose receipt is missing.

response.object: exit 0 of the committed rc3 receipt test

criteria.text: The committed rc3 Linux receipt verifies against the six check documents committed beside it.

tasks.intent: The release provider gate accepts a dispatch smoke receipt's pass scorecard on its word: evidence_refs default to empty and nothing reads the per-Run check documents. Require one check document per run_ref beside the receipt, each naming its Run with an empty breaches list, fail the gate otherwise, commit the six rc3 Linux check documents beside the committed receipt, and make the remediation command name EAWF_SMOKE_EVIDENCE_DIR and the provider of the runtime that lacks a receipt.
tasks.title: Re-check each dispatch smoke receipt against its check documents

response.object: exit 0 of the reopen unknown-head refusal test

criteria.text: eawf milestone reopen refuses with a typed reason, and writes nothing, when the repository does not hold the Milestone's accepted head commit.

response.object: exit 0 of the Linux-only disclosure search

criteria.text: The CHANGELOG 0.7.0rc3 section states that rc3 is certified and smoke-tested on Linux only.

response.object: exit 0 of the hook contract disclosure search

criteria.text: The CHANGELOG 0.7.0rc3 section names the hook contract change from session_id to run_ref and run_key.

tasks.intent: The reopen guard's tag check returns no tags when the repository lacks the accepted head, so a reopen goes through on a shallow or squashed clone. Refuse the reopen with a typed reason when the accepted head is not held locally. Then write the CHANGELOG 0.7.0rc3 lines for every fix of this revision and disclose what the section omits: rc3 is certified and smoke-tested on Linux only, the hook stdin and output carry run_ref and run_key instead of session_id, eawf init's JSON no longer has materialised_state_keys or subagent_spec_preview, and eawf config get credits a mapping key to the highest layer stating any child leaf; fix the stale session id line in the agent reports architecture page.

response.object: exit 0 of the added-lines ledger scan test

criteria.text: A diff-scoped path-leak lint over a staged generation ledger or history file flags a leak on a line the commit adds and passes a leak on a line already committed.

tasks.intent: The pre-commit path-leak lint scopes only the epoch-1 state file to the lines a commit adds, so every staged epoch-2 generation ledger is scanned whole, and a committed row the wider leak patterns now flag fails every later state commit although an append-only ledger can never change it. Scope ledger and history files under a generation to added lines on a diff-scoped scan, keep their full leak kinds, and keep the typed stores scanned in full.

criteria.text: The leak scan flags a server data-root, runtime-directory or pytest temp-root path that follows an escaped line break, tab or carriage return or an underscore, and still leaves a path after an alphanumeric or a dot alone.

response.object: exit 0 of path-leak-lint over the artifact ledger

criteria.text: No content row in the artifact ledger carries a machine path behind an escaped line break or an underscore.

tasks.intent: The server data-root, runtime-directory and pytest temp-root anchors use a lookbehind that counts the letter n and the underscore as word characters, so a path right after a JSON-escaped line break, tab or carriage return, or after an underscore, escapes both the content bound and the path-leak lint. Let those prefixes start a path while an alphanumeric or a dot before the slash still exempts it, then withhold any content row the wider scan newly flags with eawf store redact-content before the state commit.
tasks.title: Flag machine paths after an escaped line break or an underscore

response.object: exit 0 of the redaction-versus-WAL refusal test

criteria.text: eawf store redact-content refuses, and changes no ledger byte, while the native write-ahead log holds a pending or applied record whose ledger line targets the artifact ledger.

tasks.intent: Redaction rewrites an unpublished artifact-ledger line, but crash replay recognises a line only by its exact digest, so an applied or pending write-ahead-log record whose ledger line targets the artifact ledger re-appends the original leaked line at the next boot. Refuse eawf store redact-content with a typed REDACTION refusal code while any such record is unfinished, naming the record, so the operator lets recovery finish first.
tasks.title: Refuse content redaction while the WAL holds an unfinished ledger line

response.object: exit 0 of the mixed-ledger redaction test

criteria.text: A redaction plan over a ledger whose unpublished non-content line leaks still withholds every flagged content line and names each flagged non-content record key instead of refusing.

tasks.intent: A content redaction plan is refused whole when any unpublished non-content line of the artifact ledger matches a leak pattern, and the wider patterns now flag older plan and spike rows that no verb can fix. Withhold the flagged content lines anyway and list each flagged non-content record key in the answer so the operator can see what stays.
tasks.title: Redact content rows when a non-content line also leaks

response.object: exit 0 of the meter verb weighting test

criteria.text: For the same samples and cap, the budget meter verb returns the observed token total and cap verdict the native dispatch meter computes with the governor's cache_read_weight.

tasks.intent: The runtime.run.budget.meter verb folds samples with a meter at cache-read weight 1.0, while native dispatch meters the same Run with the governor's cache_read_weight, so the two disagree on whether a cache-heavy Run is over its cap. Build the verb's meter from the same governor weight dispatch uses.
tasks.title: Weight cache reads in the budget meter verb like dispatch

response.object: exit 0 of the quarantine refusal test

criteria.text: When the newest provider-fact row for a runtime and version is a quarantine, eawf release canary-export refuses that claim instead of exporting the earlier certification.

response.object: exit 0 of the expiry refusal test

criteria.text: eawf release canary-export refuses a certification whose expires_at is before the export time.

response.object: exit 0 of the re-export carry-forward test

criteria.text: A re-export of a release that already has an export keeps its isolation pair, its run_logs and the certifications of every os_class not exported this run.

tasks.intent: The canary export takes the newest row that carries a certification, so a later quarantine of the same runtime and version is skipped, an expired certification is copied as is, and a re-export of the same release keeps only its Milestones, dropping isolation, run_logs and certifications of os_classes not passed this run. Take the newest row per runtime and version whatever its outcome, refuse a quarantined or expired one with a typed reason, and carry the prior export's isolation, run_logs and other os_class records forward.
tasks.title: Export only live, unexpired certifications and keep prior evidence

response.object: exit 0 of the escape-prefix leak test

criteria.text: The proof-speed test proves that a Batch's criteria run at the same time by holding every stand-in gate at one barrier, so it fails when they run one after another and never on a slow host.

tasks.intent: test_criteria_run_at_once asserts that four one-second stand-in criteria finish in under three seconds, and a loaded CI runner took 3.91 s on macOS and 4.33 s on the devbox, so the test fails without a defect. tasks.title: Prove concurrent criteria with a barrier, not a wall-clock budget
